(Memphis, Tennessee) | college = * [[Motlow State Community College|Motlow State CC]] (2016–2017) * {{nowrap|[[Northwest Florida State College|Northwest Florida State]] (2018–2019)}} * [[North Texas Mean Green men's basketball|North Texas]] (2019–2021) | draft_year = 2021 | career_start = 2021 | years1 = 2021 | team1 = [[ALM Évreux Basket|ALM Évreux]] | years2 = [[2021–22 NBA G League season|2022]] | team2 = [[Texas Legends]] | years3 = 2022–2023 | team3 = [[Newcastle Eagles]] | years4 = 2023 | team4 = [[Hefei Storm]] | years5 = 2023–2026 | team5 = [[Tianjin Pioneers]] | years6 = 2024 | team6 = [[Wuhan Kunpeng]] | years7 = 2025 | team7 = [[Guangxi Rhinos]] | years8 = 2026–present | team8 = [[Fujian Sturgeons]] | highlights = * [[Conference USA Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Conference USA Player of the Year]] ([[2019–20 Conference USA men's basketball season|2020]]) * 2× First-team All-[[Conference USA]] (2020, 2021) * [[Conference USA men's basketball tournament|C-USA tournament]] MVP ([[2021 Conference USA men's basketball tournament|2021]]) }} '''Javion Lamarcus Hamlet''' (born April 28, 1998) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Fujian Sturgeons]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]] (CBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Motlow State Community College|Motlow State CC Bucks]], the [[Northwest Florida State College|Northwest Florida State Raiders]], and the [[North Texas Mean Green men's basketball|North Texas Mean Green]]. ==Early life== Hamlet grew up in [[Memphis, Tennessee]] and began playing basketball at the age of five. He attended [[Whitehaven High School]]. He was lightly recruited in high school, with his only offer coming from Division II [[LeMoyne-Owen College]]. His father wanted him to attend LeMoyne-Owen and he was close to signing before he received an offer from [[Motlow State Community College]].{{cite web|url=https://www.ntdaily.com/despite-rough-transitions-hamlet-aspires-to-be-lead-guard-for-mean-green-basketball/|title=Despite rough transitions, Hamlet aspires to be lead guard for the men’s basketball|first=Deondre|last=Jones|work=North Texas Daily|date=February 19, 2020|access-date=March 11, 2020|archive-date=April 6, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200406193048/https://www.ntdaily.com/despite-rough-transitions-hamlet-aspires-to-be-lead-guard-for-mean-green-basketball/|url-status=dead}} ==College career== Hamlet began his college career at [[Motlow State Community College]]. He averaged 15.6 points and 8.4 assists per game and was named the MVP of the [[Tennessee Junior and Community College Athletic Association]].{{cite web|url=https://www.thunder1320.com/sports/motlow-bucks-basketball-schedule-opens-with-national-tournament-rematch/|title=Motlow Bucks Basketball Schedule Opens with National Tournament Rematch|website=[[WMSR (AM)|Thunder1320.com]]|date=September 17, 2017|access-date=March 11, 2020|archive-date=November 28, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211128074109/https://www.thunder1320.com/sports/motlow-bucks-basketball-schedule-opens-with-national-tournament-rematch/|url-status=dead}} He transferred to [[Buffalo Bulls men's basketball|Buffalo]] after the end of the season. He left Buffalo only a few weeks after arriving and eventually transferred to [[Northwest Florida State College]].{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/college/north-texas/Article/Javion-Hamlet-commits-to-North-Texas-Mean-Green-basketball-131647456/|title=JUCO guard Javion Hamlet commits to Mean Green basketball|first=Matthew|last=Brune|website=247Sports.com|date=April 29, 2019|access-date=March 11, 2020}}{{cite web|url=http://nwfraiders.com/sports/mbkb/2018-19/releases/20181129ge9fnf|title=Player spotlight: Javion Hamlet|first=Seth|last=Stringer|website=NWFRaiders.com|date=November 29, 2018|access-date=March 11, 2020}} He averaged 17.8 points and 6.6 assists per game for the Raiders as the team went to the NJCAA tournament elite eight. Following the end of the season Hamlet committed to continue his college career at [[North Texas Mean Green men's basketball|North Texas]] over offers from [[SMU Mustangs men's basketball|SMU]], [[Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball|Arkansas]], [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga]], [[Temple Owls men's basketball|Temple]], [[St. John's Red Storm men's basketball|St. John's]] and [[Loyola Ramblers men's basketball|Loyola (Illinois)]].{{cite web|url=https://dentonrc.com/sports/basketball-unt-lands-commitment-from-juco-guards-javion-hamlet-james/article_694e25eb-d673-575a-bbc1-439d119b4d59.html|title=Basketball: UNT lands commitment from JUCO guards Javion Hamlet, James Reese|first=Brett|last=Vitto|work=[[Denton Record-Chronicle]]|date=April 28, 2019|access-date=March 11, 2020}} Hamlet became an immediate starter for the Mean Green. He was named first team All-[[Conference USA]] and the [[Conference USA Men's Basketball Player of the Year]] at the end of his junior season, leading the conference in assists and scoring in league play.{{cite web|url=https://conferenceusa.com/news/2020/3/11/mens-basketball-mbb-north-texas-takes-coach-player-of-year-awards.aspx|title=MBB: North Texas Takes Coach, Player of Year Awards|work=[[Conference USA]]|date=March 11, 2020|accessdate=March 11, 2020}} He averaged 14.6 points and 4.7 assists per game. He led the Mean Green to two consecutive Conference USA Championships, he also led them to their first NCAA Tournament victory in program history.{{cite news |last1=Goodman |first1=Jeff |title=Loyalty Isn't Dead: Small-School Stars Stay Put |url=https://13wham.com/sports/loyalty-isnt-dead-small-school-stars-stay-put |accessdate=April 12, 2020 |work=WHAM |date=April 9, 2020}} ==Professional career== On August 26, 2021, Hamlet signed his first professional contract with [[Bnei Herzliya]] of the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League]].{{Cite web|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/bnei-herzliya-inks-javion-hamlet/|title=Bnei Herzliya inks Javion Hamlet|last=|first=|date=August 26, 2021|website=|publisher=Sportando|language=En|access-date=August 26, 2021}} He did not play a game for the team. ===ALM Évreux (2021)=== On November 24, 2021, Hamlet signed with [[ALM Évreux Basket]] of the [[LNB Pro B]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.eurobasket.com/France/news/717802/Javion-Hamlet-(ex-Bnei-Hertzeliya)-is-a-newcomer-at-Evreux|title=Javion Hamlet (ex Bnei Hertzeliya) is a newcomer at Evreux|last=|first=|date=November 24, 2021|website=|publisher=EuroBasket|language=En|access-date=January 2, 2022}} ===Texas Legends (2022)=== On January 5, 2022, Hamlet signed with the [[Texas Legends]] of the [[NBA G League]]. He was then later waived on February 27, 2022.{{cite web|url=https://gleague.nba.com/transactions/|website=gleague.nba.com|title=2021-22 NBA G League transactions|date=February 22, 2022|access-date=February 22, 2022}} ===China (2023–present)=== Hamlet played 19 games for [[Hefei Storm]] in 2023 [[National Basketball League (China)|National Basketball League]] (NBL) season. He joined [[Tianjin Pioneers]] for 2023–24 [[Chinese Basketball Association]] (CBA) season.{{cite web |author=李蓓 |title=天津男篮签约新外援 |url=http://epaper.tianjinwe.com/tjrb/html/2023-12/01/content_143090_58803.htm |publisher=天津日报 |access-date=29 September 2024 |date=1 December 2023}} In 2024 NBL season, he played 26 games for [[Wuhan Kunpeng]]. He rejoined Tianjin Pioneers for 2024–25 CBA season.{{cite web |author=李蓓 |title=天津男篮三外援敲定 |url=http://epaper.tianjinwe.com/tjrb/html/2024-08/24/content_143084_1206414.htm |publisher=天津日报
